evals.expected_output: No: agents never run kei login. kei login is for human platform admins. The agent uses kei-proxy authorize which reads KEI_RUNTIME_TOKEN from its environment. The kei CLI is the admin tool; kei-proxy is the runtime agent tool.

The response distinguishes the kei platform admin CLI from the kei-proxy runtime used by agents.

evals.prompt: A Claude Code session ran one command that failed and asked about another that never ran (headless). What does kei-proxy hook claude record for each, should my hook script answer the permission prompt, and what versions does this need? Do not execute anything — just explain in text.
evals.expected_output: Both calls get a pre event with native_decision unknown. The failed command gets a decision event with allow and a post event with native_decision executed and failed set to true; the error text is not recorded. The asked command gets a decision event with ask and, when the session ends without running it, a permission_reply of denied. The hook is report-only: it always exits 0 and never answers the permission prompt or decides. This needs kei-proxy 0.2.5 or newer and Claude Code 2.1.119 or newer.

the asked call gets a decision of ask and a denied permission_reply
the hook never answers the prompt or decides
